title: The Bursar of the Drowning Crypt
story: Beneath the salt cliffs, Mr 6 finds 14 marsh families huddled on a ledge while Murrowfane, a barnacled accountant-eel, guards the crypt's emergency hoard of 1,260 moonstone shards. "Nobody leaves until the ledger balances," it gurgles, flicking an abacus with its tail. Murrowfane claims a 30% keeper's tithe, and the rest must be split evenly among the families so each can buy passage on the cliff-ferry.
question: After Murrowfane takes its 30% tithe, how many moonstone shards does each of the 14 families receive?
solution: The tithe is 30% of 1260 = 378 shards, so 1260 - 378 = 882 shards remain.
praise: Splitting the hoard by 14 was exactly the right move — the tithe just needed to come off the top before the sharing.
hint: First find what's LEFT after the 30% tithe, then split that leftover among the 14 families.
victory: Mr 6 recited the number before the eel's abacus had stopped clicking. Murrowfane, outbalanced by a six, stamped the ledger "SETTLED" and slithered off to audit something quieter.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight holds up a glowing moonstone shard before a barnacle-crusted eel accountant with an abacus, in a sea-cave crypt lit by green tide-light with rescued families on a stone ledge.
